nodes.label: relay_pair_id 32-bit width bug
nodes.rationale: Re-graded from 'permanent fail-closed outage' to a probabilistic, self-healing mutual-exclusion fault, sticky only on single-relay fabrics: teardown frees the slot, multi-relay round-robin routes the loser elsewhere, and re-enrollment mints a new key. The fix is ~5 lines (raw digest[..8]) and orthogonal to the mux wire break.

nodes.label: Same-owner registration collision silently replaces and cross-wires
nodes.rationale: The rejection only fires when existing.owner != cert_identity, so K(A,B) vs K(A,D) falls through to insert; the gateway discards the src header, so datagrams land on the wrong leg and boringtun roams the endpoint. The only silent branch.

nodes.label: LIVE HOLE — any enrolled gateway can inject into any pair's relay slot
nodes.rationale: Only the receive side is enforced — a slot can only be created by the cert holder — while the send side is unenforced and identities gw-<rowid> are trivially enumerable. WireGuard E2E holds so this is DoS/reachability, not confidentiality. Fixed by dropping (never closing) any dest other than the one legal registration key: closing buys nothing against a reconnecting attacker and costs the relay more than the compare.

nodes.label: 32-bit pair key is adversarially preimage-attackable (peer_identity is not cert-bound)
nodes.rationale: serve enforces my_identity == cert_identity and never checks the peer half, which is free-form wire input; a 32-bit target preimage is minutes on a laptop, letting one compromised gateway occupy a chosen pair's slot, lock the rightful owner out, and receive its datagrams. 'Collision-safe at v1 scale' was true for accidents and false adversarially.

nodes.label: LIVE GAP — a peer that leaves the relay pins the path in Relayed forever
nodes.rationale: There is no per-pair idle death — max_idle_timeout is connection-scoped — and the Relayed arm has no liveness requirement beyond connection health, so peer absence is structurally undetectable. Worse, it is self-perpetuating: the survivor discards every punch directive while relay_pointed holds, so the pin prevents the very event that would clear it.

nodes.label: The stale-pin sweep breaks in both directions under a shared connection
nodes.rationale: Collect gets a false negative (healthy_relay becomes 'shared conn alive' for every peer, so the sweep silently stops firing for exactly the leak it was built to catch) and Act becomes a fabric-wide outage (teardown closes the shared connection). Requires per-peer route presence plus splitting teardown into drop_peer_route and close_shared_conn.

nodes.label: The /0 ALPN deprecation horizon has no valid anchor
nodes.rationale: X-6 does not exist and would be the wrong instrument anyway — it tracks gateway versions at the controller while the deciding entity is the relay, and a version does not say which ALPN was negotiated. A per-relay ALPN counter is necessary but not fleet-complete, since a relay only sees the gateways that chose it.

nodes.label: Width change is a lockstep upgrade: relays first, then gateways
nodes.rationale: Three parties recompute the derivation independently, so a version split means the pair silently never rendezvouses. No compatibility shim deliberately: a dual-derivation relay would accept BOTH keys, re-opening the 32-bit slot to an attacker for as long as it is supported.
